properties.description:
Cut 2026-10-28 on Anthony's word ("Let's continue with the release", version 0.93.1 his choice), in PR release/v0.93.1. The tag push stays his. A patch carrying:
- #811: a --registry-root server raises its soft RLIMIT_NOFILE to the hard limit as it starts and says so; it checks --registry-max-open x 76 files a design (64 table files + 12) + 32 of its own against the limit and prints one WARNING naming the numbers and what to change when they do not fit, and keeps serving; GET /readyz gains a second line "open files: N of M allowed (K left)" and the headers x-reflow2-open-files / x-reflow2-open-file-limit, status code and first line unchanged.

Measured against the published 0.93.0 binary (linux-x86_64 archive sha256 3a889ee7..., checked against checksums.txt): 199 tools on both, none added, removed or changed (every tool byte-equal in name, description and schema; toolsnap: all 199 match). Skills 35 on both, none changed; list_skills and get_instructions unchanged. Nothing deprecated or removed. The schema stamp does not move (28 node, 69 edge types, enum vocabularies equal; describe_schema identical), so no upgrade doc is owed. Checked on the 0.93.1 build: /readyz on a one-design --http server answers the open-files line and both headers (0.93.0: first line only); a registry started at soft 256 / hard 4096 raised itself to 4096 (0.93.0 stayed at 256); held at 512 with --registry-max-open 64 it warned of up to 4,896 files and kept serving. The --call setup gains nothing and loses nothing. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
properties.name: v0.93.1 — a server holding many designs raises its open-file limit, warns when they may not fit, and /readyz says the headroom
